comments.body:
Thanks, Alex — this is a useful fix. Reporting the actual token usage and distinguishing `max_tokens` from a normal finish both make sense. I reviewed `c2509a2` and ran 69 related tests locally; they all passed.

Could you address two edge cases before we merge?

1. **Reset stream metadata for each authentication attempt.** `stream_meta` is currently initialized outside the auth loop in `_stream_chat_events()`. I reproduced a first attempt that emits `message_start` with 250 input / 1 output tokens, then an error before any text. The fallback authentication attempt succeeds with text but no usage events, and the final response incorrectly reports 250 / 1 / 251 from the failed attempt. Please initialize the metadata inside each attempt so a successful response without usage events gets the documented zero fallback. A mocked regression test covering that sequence would help.

2. **Await inner-stream cleanup when the caller closes early.** The new `stream_chat_completion()` wrapper iterates over `_stream_chat_events()` without explicitly closing it. After consuming one text chunk and awaiting `stream.aclose()`, I found that the HTTP response and session were still open. On the base branch, both were closed before that call returned; with this change, cleanup was deferred to async-generator finalization. Could you wrap the inner iterator with `contextlib.aclosing()` (or equivalent explicit cleanup) and add a test asserting that both contexts have exited when `aclose()` returns?

The build and validation checks are green. These two cases came from additional mocked checks; no live paid API requests were made. Thanks for taking a look!

Addressed both cases: metadata is now initialized per authentication attempt, and the public streaming wrapper uses contextlib.aclosing to await inner-stream cleanup. Added mocked regressions for the failed-attempt 250/1 usage followed by a successful response without usage, and for response/session cleanup completing before aclose returns. Both failed before this fix; all 22 related tests now pass. No live API requests were made.

This comment was drafted with Claude Code.
